title: Call 911
summary: For any life-threatening emergency in the U.S.: not breathing, severe bleeding, chest pain, stroke signs, fire, immediate danger.
steps: Get to a safe place if you can do it without delay.
Call 911. If you cannot speak, text 911 where supported: call if you can, text if you can't.
Say WHERE you are first: address, cross streets, landmarks.
Say what happened and how many people are hurt.
Stay on the line. Follow the dispatcher's instructions.
If the call fails: try again, move to a spot with better signal, or send a text.
dont: Do not hang up before the dispatcher says to.
Do not call 911 to ask about power outages or storm information.
warn: Texting to 911 is not available everywhere. Voice calls are still the most reliable.

title: Severe Bleeding
summary: Call 911, press hard on the wound, use a tourniquet for life-threatening limb bleeding.
steps: Call 911 (or have someone call). Put on gloves if you have them.
Press hard directly on the wound with a clean cloth. Use both hands.
Soaked through? Do NOT remove it. Add more cloth and keep pressing.
Limb bleeding you cannot control: put a tourniquet 2–3 inches above the wound, not on a joint. Tighten until bleeding stops.
Write down the time the tourniquet went on. Leave it on.
Keep the person lying down and warm. Watch for shock.
dont: Do not remove objects stuck in the wound.
Do not loosen or remove a tourniquet.
Do not stop pressing to look at the wound.
warn: Pale, cold, clammy, confused or faint means shock. Keep calling for help.

title: No Breathing: CPR and AED
summary: Unresponsive and not breathing normally: call 911 and start hands-only CPR.
steps: Tap shoulders and shout. Not responding and not breathing normally (or only gasping)?
Call 911 and put the phone on speaker. Send someone for an AED.
Place the heel of your hand on the center of the chest, other hand on top.
Push hard and fast: at least 2 inches (5 cm) deep, 100 to 120 per minute. Let the chest rise fully.
AED arrives: turn it on and follow the voice prompts. Keep clear while it analyzes or shocks.
Do not stop until help takes over or the person moves.
dont: Do not stop to check for a pulse for more than a few seconds.
Do not worry about hurting them. Not doing CPR is worse.
warn: Children and infants: if trained, give breaths too. Infant: two fingers, about 1.5 inches (4 cm) deep.

title: Choking
summary: Cannot speak, cough or breathe: call 911 and give back blows and thrusts.
steps: Can they cough hard? Let them cough. Stay with them.
Cannot speak, cough or breathe? Have someone call 911.
Adult or child: Red Cross teaches 5 back blows, then 5 abdominal thrusts, and repeat. (AHA teaches abdominal thrusts.)
Infant under 1: face down on your forearm, 5 back blows, then face up, 5 chest thrusts with two fingers.
Pregnant or very large person: do chest thrusts, not abdominal.
If they pass out: lay them down and start CPR. Look in the mouth before breaths.
dont: Do not do blind finger sweeps.
Do not give back blows to someone who is coughing forcefully.
warn: Anyone who was choked should be checked by a medical professional afterward.

title: Severe Allergic Reaction
summary: Trouble breathing or swelling after a sting, food or medication: epinephrine first, then 911.
steps: Use the person's epinephrine auto-injector RIGHT AWAY if they have one. Follow the device instructions.
Call 911, even if they seem better.
Lie flat with legs raised. Sit up if breathing is hard. Side if vomiting.
Another dose may be needed. Follow the prescriber's and dispatcher's instructions.
Stay with them. If they stop breathing, start CPR.
Give the used injector to the responders.
dont: Do not wait to see if it gets better.
Do not rely on an antihistamine alone.
Do not let them stand or walk.
warn: Signs: swollen lips or tongue, wheezing, hives all over, dizziness, vomiting after exposure.

title: Stroke or Heart Attack
summary: Face drooping, weak arm, slurred speech, or chest pressure: call 911 immediately.
steps: Stroke, BE FAST: Balance loss, Eyes (vision loss), Face droop, Arm weakness, Speech trouble, Time to call 911.
Heart attack: chest pressure or pain, short of breath, cold sweat, pain in arm, jaw or back.
Call 911 now. Do not drive yourself.
Note the time the symptoms began.
Unlock the door. Sit or lie comfortably. Stay calm.
Follow the dispatcher. If the person collapses and is not breathing normally, start CPR.
dont: Do not wait to see if it passes.
Do not give medicine unless the dispatcher or clinician tells you to.
warn: Women, older adults and people with diabetes may have milder or unusual signs.

title: Burns
summary: Cool with cool running water for at least 10 minutes. Know which burns need 911.
steps: Stop the burning. Remove rings and clothing near the burn, unless stuck.
Cool with cool (not ice-cold) running water for at least 10 minutes, up to about 20.
Cover loosely with a clean nonstick dressing or clean plastic wrap.
Keep the person warm. Watch for shock.
Chemical burn: flush with lots of running water for at least 20 minutes.
Call 911 for burns to face, hands, feet, groin or joints, large or deep burns, and chemical or electrical burns.
dont: Do not use ice, butter, oil or toothpaste.
Do not break blisters.
Do not pull off stuck clothing.
warn: Electrical burns need medical evaluation. Make sure power is off before touching the person.

title: Poisoning or Overdose
summary: Call Poison Help 1-800-222-1222, or 911 if the person is unconscious, seizing or struggling to breathe.
steps: Unconscious, seizing or hard to wake, or struggling to breathe? Call 911.
Otherwise call Poison Help: 1-800-222-1222 (U.S., free, 24 hours).
Have the container, the person's age and weight, and the time ready.
Gas or fumes: get to fresh air first.
Skin: remove contaminated clothing and rinse with running water for 15 to 20 minutes.
Eyes: flush gently with clean water for at least 15 minutes.
dont: Do not make the person vomit.
Do not give anything to eat or drink unless told to.
warn: If the line is busy or there is no service, call 911.

title: Carbon Monoxide
summary: Alarm sounding, or headache, dizziness and nausea near a generator, stove or heater: get outside now.
steps: Get everyone outside into fresh air immediately. Do not stop to collect things.
Call 911 from outside.
Do not go back in until responders say it is safe.
Everyone exposed needs medical care, even if they feel better.
Later: find and fix the source before using it again.
dont: Do not run generators, grills, camp stoves or heaters indoors, in garages or near windows.
Do not rely on opening a window.
warn: Carbon monoxide has no smell. People who are asleep may not wake up. Use battery-powered CO alarms.

title: House Fire
summary: Get out, stay out, call 911 from outside.
steps: Get out. Use your planned exit. Take no belongings.
Stay low under smoke where the air is cleaner.
Feel doors with the back of your hand. Hot? Use another way out.
Close doors behind you to slow the fire.
Go to your outside meeting place. Count everyone.
Call 911 from outside. Tell firefighters if anyone is missing.
dont: Do not go back inside for people, pets or things.
Do not use elevators.
warn: Clothes on fire: stop, drop, roll. Trapped: close the door, seal gaps with towels, signal at a window, call 911.

title: Tornado Warning
summary: Take shelter now: lowest floor, interior room, no windows.
steps: Go now to a basement, storm cellar or lowest-floor interior room.
Stay away from windows, doors and outside walls.
Get low. Cover your head and neck with your arms, a mattress, blankets or a helmet.
Mobile or manufactured home? Leave and get to a sturdy building before the storm.
In a vehicle: do not try to outrun it in traffic. Reach a sturdy building if you can. Otherwise park, buckle up, head below the windows, cover your head.
Stay put until the warning ends. Then check for injuries and hazards.
dont: Do not open windows.
Do not shelter under an overpass.
Do not wait to see it.
warn: Watch means be ready. Warning means a tornado is happening or imminent.

title: Thunderstorm and Lightning
summary: When thunder roars, go indoors. Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder.
steps: Go inside a fully enclosed building or a hard-topped vehicle with the windows up.
Stay away from windows, plumbing, corded phones and plugged-in electronics.
No showers, baths or dishes during the storm.
Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back out.
Caught outside: avoid open fields, hilltops, tall isolated trees, water and metal. No place outdoors is safe.
dont: Do not shelter under a tree or in a tent, shed or pavilion.
Do not go back out as soon as the rain stops.
warn: Lightning victims do not carry a charge. Call 911 and start CPR if needed.

title: Flood
summary: Move to higher ground. Turn around, don't drown.
steps: Move to higher ground now. Do not wait for instructions if water is rising.
Never walk, swim or drive through floodwater. Six inches of moving water can knock you down.
If trapped in a building, go to the highest floor. Do not go into a closed attic. Call 911 and signal for help.
Car in rising water: leave it and move to higher ground if you can do so safely.
Stay off bridges over fast water. Stay away from downed power lines.
After: floodwater is contaminated. Do not drink or use tap water until cleared.
dont: Do not touch electrical equipment if you are wet or standing in water.
Do not drive around barricades.
warn: Flash floods can arrive in minutes. A watch means be prepared; a warning means move now.

title: Earthquake
summary: Drop, Cover and Hold On. Do not run outside.
steps: DROP to your hands and knees.
COVER your head and neck under a sturdy table, or against an interior wall.
HOLD ON until the shaking stops.
In bed: stay there and cover your head with a pillow.
Outdoors: move to an open area away from buildings, trees and wires. Driving: pull over, stay in the car.
After: check for injuries and gas leaks. Expect aftershocks and repeat Drop, Cover, Hold On.
dont: Do not run outside during the shaking.
Do not stand in a doorway.
Do not use matches or lighters if you smell gas.
warn: Near the coast: if shaking was strong or lasted 20 seconds or more, or you get a tsunami warning, move inland or to high ground on foot at once.

title: Wildfire
summary: When told to evacuate, leave immediately. Protect your lungs from smoke.
steps: Leave immediately when told. Do not wait to see flames.
Take go-bags, medications, documents, pets and chargers.
Wear an N95 respirator and long sleeves if smoke is present.
If time allows: close windows and doors, turn off gas, turn on outdoor lights.
Follow official routes. Drive with headlights on.
Trapped: call 911, stay in the car or a clear area, cover up with blankets. Do not run through flames.
dont: Do not use cloth or surgical masks for smoke.
Do not return until officials say it is safe.
warn: Burned slopes can flood or slide when it rains. Stay alert after the fire.

title: Hurricane
summary: Leave when ordered. Storm surge is the deadliest part.
steps: Know your evacuation zone. Leave when told, before the winds arrive.
Staying in a safe building: go to an interior room on the lowest floor that will not flood, away from windows.
Keep a battery radio on. Do not go outside during the calm eye.
Water coming in? Move to an upper floor. Take tools to exit an attic.
Never use a generator, grill or camp stove indoors.
After: stay out of floodwater and away from downed lines.
dont: Do not wait to see how bad it gets.
Do not drive through water.
warn: The category number measures wind only. Surge and rain cause most deaths.

title: Heat Stroke and Heat Exhaustion
summary: Confusion, very hot skin or fainting in the heat: call 911 and cool the person fast.
steps: Heat stroke signs: 103°F (39.4°C) or higher, confusion, hot red or damp skin, fainting. Call 911.
Move the person to shade or air conditioning.
Cool quickly: cold water or ice bath if possible, wet sheets, ice packs at neck, armpits and groin, fanning.
Do not give drinks if they are confused or unconscious.
Heat exhaustion (heavy sweating, cool clammy skin, nausea): move to a cool place, loosen clothes, cool cloths, sip water.
Get medical help if vomiting or not better in about an hour.
dont: Never leave a child, pet or anyone in a parked car.
Do not wait for symptoms to get worse.
warn: Heat stroke can cause permanent harm or death. Treat it as an emergency every time.

title: Hypothermia and Frostbite
summary: Get out of the cold, remove wet clothes and warm the center of the body.
steps: Call 911 for severe cases: confusion, very slow breathing, no shivering, unresponsive.
Move to a warm, dry place. Handle gently.
Remove wet clothing. Cover with dry blankets, including head and neck.
Warm the chest, neck, head and groin first, using warm (not hot) wrapped packs or body heat.
If alert and able to swallow: warm, sweet, non-alcoholic drinks.
Frostbite: warm in warm (not hot) water. Do not rub. Seek medical care.
dont: Do not give alcohol.
Do not use direct heat like heating pads or fires.
Do not rub arms and legs.
warn: Hypothermia can happen indoors in a cold house and in cool wet weather above freezing.

title: Power Outage
summary: Light, food safety, heat and carbon monoxide are the big four.
steps: Report the outage to your utility. Check on neighbors.
Use flashlights, not candles.
Keep the fridge and freezer closed: about 4 hours in the fridge, about 48 hours in a full freezer.
Generators go outdoors only, at least 20 feet from the house, with CO alarms inside.
Downed power line: stay at least 35 feet away and call 911.
Medical equipment needing power? Use your backup plan or go to a place with power.
dont: Do not use grills, camp stoves or generators indoors.
Do not eat perishable food that was above 40°F (4°C) for over 2 hours.
warn: Cold or hot homes are dangerous for babies, older adults and people with health conditions. Leave if you cannot stay safe.

title: Evacuate Now
summary: Told to leave? Go now with people, pets, medicines, documents and chargers.
steps: Leave when ordered. Delay costs lives.
Grab go-bags, medications, ID and insurance papers, phone and chargers, cash.
Take pets in carriers. Wear sturdy shoes.
Follow official routes. Keep the radio on.
Lock up. Turn off utilities only if told to.
Tell your out-of-area contact where you are going.
dont: Do not drive through floodwater or smoke you cannot see through.
Do not go back for belongings.
warn: Official orders override your own plan.

title: Phones Down: Emergency Communication
summary: Text, conserve battery and use radio. Use your family plan.
steps: Text instead of calling. Texts often go through when calls fail.
Keep messages short: where you are, that you are OK, where you will wait.
Contact your out-of-area person. Everyone checks in there.
Save battery: low power mode, airplane mode between check-ins, lower brightness.
Listen on a NOAA Weather Radio or AM/FM radio for alerts and instructions.
No contact? Go to your agreed meeting place.
dont: Do not call 911 for information or to report an outage.
Do not post your exact location or that your home is empty.
warn: Keep calls short. Free the lines for emergencies.
